ADO Boards client: named-field checks, hostallow then CheckADOBaseURL before Getenv; screened doRaw with one api-version, Basic :PAT or Bearer, no redirects, scrubbed bodies

ParentLinker: Hierarchy-Reverse on the child, replace-in-one rev-tested PATCH; LinkIssues adds Related; both read-first and idempotent

findings.text: Two files are changed but not in the task's files list: internal/cmd/inert_config_test.go (the four inertKeyReasons entries, which TestNoSettableKeyIsInert needs, and they are well argued) and ARCHITECTURE.md (line-ref refresh).

ARCHITECTURE.md refreshes the project/project.go refs (Save :538, saveLossless :553) but leaves the enumKeys bullet saying 'five dotted keys' (now six) and pointing at internal/cmd/project.go:325 / :339. This diff moved enumKeys to :335 and checkEnumValue to :350.

In TestBoardADOKeysAbsentSaveByteIdentical, the Load-then-Save byte-identical half cannot catch a missing omitempty: Save diffs the loaded value against an identical value, so a zero field yields no op either way. Only the fresh-document half actually guards the 'zero value leaks into the file' contract.

board.auth_scheme is gated on the full configenum.AuthSchemes set, so private-token and basic are accepted even though the locked board_config allows only the PAT-via-Basic default or bearer. The task says to check against AuthSchemes, and doctor's combination check is assigned to t-11.
TestBoardDoesNotInheritRemote only shows that the loader and readDotted don't inherit, which holds trivially today. The real inheritance risk is boardsync.Config, which lands in t-16.

assets/prompts/options.md does not cover the four new board.* keys yet, while its own text says to stop on any `dross project show` field it does not cover. No test enforces per-key coverage; this is presumably owned by a sibling docs task.

The 'milestone branch' subtest of TestProtectedADOBaseRoutesThroughChorePR ignores the branches stubADOProtection records, and the stub says protected for any branch. If readBaseProtection asked about the wrong branch (say main instead of milestone/v1.8), the ADO tests would still pass. Asserting *asked == ["milestone/v1.8"] would catch it.

baseProtection.Checked is set but never read. routeBaseChores gates on protectionReadable(), which repeats readBaseProtection's provider switch. If the two drift apart the result is safe (the zero value reads as unknown and the push is refused), but one of them could go.
When [remote].auth_env is empty, the ADO fix text says "check the PAT in $<unset> ([remote].auth_env)", which reads oddly. It is harmless, because resolveToken has no default env var.
choreState (ship.go) still reports "auto-merge" in ship --json for an armed ADO chore PR. That is a stable enum value, and this task does not claim it.

readBaseProtection's azure-devops Fix always points at the PAT in [remote].auth_env, even when the unknown read came from a refused api_base host or a possibly truncated policy list; Reason carries the real cause, so the message is only partly misleading
pullURL infers Azure Repos only from '/_git/', so an SSH-form ADO remote (git@ssh.dev.azure.com:v3/o/p/r) would still get a GitHub-shaped /pull/<n> link; fine while [remote].url is the https form
choreState (ship --json) still reports "auto-merge" for an armed ADO chore PR; this task does not claim it, and only the human narration was in scope

The doctor.go wiring has no doctor-level test: no doctor_test case sets board.auth_scheme. BoardCombination takes four plain string arguments in a row, so if the call site swapped b.AuthUser and b.AuthScheme, the diag tests would still pass.

azureBoardsCombination warns on any non-empty milestone_mode, including a globally invalid one that doctor already hard-fails at the board section. The existing milestone check deliberately skips globally invalid modes, so this arm reports twice on a key it calls ignored.
The non-ADO 'no effect' warning interpolates the provider after normalising it, so an empty provider renders as 'on a  board'. That case is already a hard failure, so it is cosmetic only.

ListIssues with no labels (dross watch and an unlabelled issue pull both call it with State open only) runs a WIQL query with no state predicate. It reads every work item in the project, closed history included, and then filters by state category on the client. Past 20,000 items, ADO's WIQL limit (VS402337) makes every unlabelled pull fail with an error on large projects. That is reported correctly, never as zero, but the cost and the cap are worth addressing, for example by excluding the known Completed/Removed state names in WIQL or using $top with paging.

The '[System.TeamProject] = @project' and project-scoped path assertions (wiqlQueries) only exercise ListIssues. The EnsureMilestoneEpic WIQL is covered structurally, because it shares queryIDs and the mock server rejects any other path, but no test asserts it directly.

The contract wording says 'open omits Done and Removed'. The test uses Agile's 'Closed' state, which is in the Completed category. The filter works by category, so this is equivalent, but a Scrum/Basic 'Done' case is not exercised.

UpdateIssue with only a Milestone takes the no-op path straight to GetIssue, so the 'no relation op on update' loop in TestADOCreateIssueParentEpic currently sees no PATCH at all. It would still catch a regression that sent one.

SetState treats every HTTP 400 on the state PATCH as a rule rejection to warn about and skip, not just TF401320. A 400 for any other reason, such as a malformed request, would be quietly skipped during sync. This matches what the description asks for, so it is recorded only.

In TestADOSetStateOverride 'an override beats the default', the in-progress->Doing row on Basic Issue gives the same result as the default, so that row cannot tell an ignored override from an honoured one. The planned->Doing row (default To Do) is the one that actually tests the override.

In TestADOCloseIssueAsVerifies 'a 200 that did not take', the read-back is Committed, not the Active the contract names, because the Scrum PBI fixture has no Active state. It tests the same failure (an InProgress-category read-back after a 200), and the error is checked for 'work item 42' and the written state 'Done'.

choreWaitHint tells the user on azure-devops that auto-complete will complete the chore PR, but waitForMilestoneChores also fires when this run's chore PR is Manual (auto-complete could not be set). The narration printed just before (milestone.go:273) says 'complete it by hand', so the two messages contradict each other. The same happens for a PR an earlier run left open, where dross does not know whether auto-complete is armed. Consider checking head.ChorePR.Manual, or using neutral wording.

Doc comments in internal/cmd/milestone.go are now out of date. routeMilestoneHead still says 'With commits ahead on a GitHub remote... Unprotected, and every other forge, keep the policy below', and routeProtectedMilestone still says routed is false 'off GitHub'. Both now cover Azure DevOps too.

The azure-devops row of TestMilestoneHeadLegacyTable (milestone_protected_test.go) now passes only because TestMain's hermetic ADOBranchProtectionFunc stub answers known-and-unprotected. The test's comment 'only GitHub is ever asked about protection' no longer matches what the code does.

waitForMilestoneChores gates the open-chore-PR lookup on readBaseProtection(...).Protected, so when nothing is ahead and the ADO policy read is unknown (401, refused host, truncated list) it returns nil and lets the integration PR open even if an earlier run's chore PR into the milestone branch is still open. A read that failed is treated here as unprotected. GitHub already behaved this way; this change extends it to azure-devops.

choreWaitHint keeps GitHub's 'merge it (it merges itself once allowed)' even when this run's PR could not be armed (Manual); only the azure-devops branch uses the armed flag. Pre-existing wording, deliberately preserved.

The unchanged TestMilestoneHeadLegacyTable azure-devops row now reaches readBaseProtection and relies on TestMain's global ADOBranchProtectionFunc stub (known, unprotected) to keep today's push; that dependency is pinned by TestHermeticBranchProtection_NeverDials.

Two comments still list the old provider set: NewBoard's doc comment in internal/forge/forge.go (lines 257-261) does not mention azure-devops, and the Board.Provider field comment in internal/project/project.go:287 still reads 'forgejo | gitea | gitlab | youtrack | jira | github'.

Its natural home would be next to TestNewBoardNormalisesProvider in internal/forge/forge_test.go, but keeping it in enum_divergence_test.go stays within the task's declared files.

In TestADOPhaseCloseReadBack 'one refused task close strands no other', the check that work item 12's last state PATCH is Done passes from setBoardState's task-complete PATCH alone. CloseIssueAs then sees the item already Done and sends no write, so task 12 never gets a close PATCH as such. The test still fails if the loop stops at the first refusal, because t-2 would never be created. But it cannot tell whether t-2's close ran, and its message ('want its close to Done') describes the wrong PATCH.

With --close, the ADO path now runs SetState and then CloseIssueAs, the same pattern as Jira and YouTrack. If the workflow keeps the item where it is, the item gets two identical System.State PATCHes. If state_map.complete names a state outside the Completed category, SetState writes it before CloseIssueAs refuses it. So the CloseIssue arm's comment ('refuses ... before writing') does not hold for the command as a whole, even though it still errors and prints no '(closed)'.
The CloseIssue doc comment in phase.go now wraps as 'never a' / 'three-name allowlist' / 'of the flat boards' across three lines. The line it was folded into should be reflowed.

azureboards_state_sync_test.go reads tr.calls (TestConfigCarriesADOFields) and writes tr.stick / tr.stickOnce / tr.items (TestADOPhaseCloseReadBack, TestBoardClientArmsRouteByType) without tr.mu, while the other helpers take the lock. It is safe because no request is in flight at those points, but taking the lock everywhere would be more consistent.
The reflowed CloseIssue doc comment in phase.go leaves a short line ('// github.go's toIssue') in the middle of a sentence. Cosmetic only.

phase.go re-parents whenever the client satisfies forge.ParentLinker, passing it milestoneID. What that number means differs by backend: on Jira it is a project version id, on the forges a milestone id. Only AzureBoardsClient implements ParentLinker today, so nothing is wrong yet. But a backend that adds ParentLinker later (Jira epics, GitLab) would quietly link phases under whatever issue has that number. Checking for *forge.AzureBoardsClient here, or having EnsureMilestoneLink say whether its id is a work item, would close that gap.

reap.go's classifyMilestoneMirrors uses CheckMilestoneClosable as its gate, so letting Azure Boards through also makes Azure Boards milestone Epics reapable. Those closes go through the verified CloseIssue, so the behaviour is consistent, but no test covers this path.
TestLinkerOnlyBoardStillRelatesTasks checks the number of links and the parent end (PROJ-100), but not that the child end is a different task key each time.

In SyncTasks, a task whose close is refused (TaskCloseError) hits continue before LinkParent, so it stays without a parent for that run. This ordering is older than this diff, and the next sync fixes it.
phase.go's warning when re-parenting the phase item fails (LinkParent error on the update edge) has no test; only the task-level link fault is exercised

TestADOBacklogRelatesRoutedItem's re-run check counts only System.LinkTypes.Related PATCHes, while the test_contract says a second SyncBacklog sends zero relation PATCH; a repeated Hierarchy-Reverse or other relation write on the second sync would go unseen

TestADOReapUndoRestoresPriorState guards the state restore against vacuity (it fails if Apply left the state unchanged) but not the tag restore: it never checks that Apply actually rewrote dross/status:uat. relabelReapedCard only warns when it fails, so if the sweep stopped relabelling, the 'prior tags' assertion would pass without testing anything.

If a parent link is refused at finalize it is only warned about. A later FinalizePhase will not retry it, because the path for existing cards (finalizeCard) never sets a parent, so only a later SyncTasks repairs the orphan. The warning text does not promise a retry, so the behaviour is honest.
Undo's returned error gives only a count; the refused id appears on stderr, and that is where the refused-restore subtest checks for it. This matches the existing reap_undo design.

If LinkParent fails for a card created at finalize, the card is still closed and recorded in board.json. A later FinalizePhase resolves it by key and goes through finalizeCard, which never calls LinkParent, and once the phase is complete task sync is unlikely to run again. So the orphan is permanent, and the warning doesn't say a retry is coming (it doesn't claim one either).

For the refused restore, the contract says 'Undo errors naming that id', but Undo's returned error only gives a count ('1 of 2 card(s) could not be restored'). Id 21 is named on stderr, and that is what the test checks. This matches Undo's existing design, but the error value itself never names the item.

TestADOFinalizeTasksThenPhase checks 'reads back Completed' through the tracker's stored state (Done), not what the client read back. The client-side read-back check is covered separately by TestADOFinalizeReportsRefusedTaskClose.

A regression that drops $expand=relations from getWorkItem/readItems, or drops auth, would still pass every command test on this fake.

The test scopes its checks to section 12 and to each key's own bullet, so the overlapping `7.1`/`bearer` wording in the remote.* bullets cannot satisfy it vacuously.

If the exactly-once check were weakened (e.g. seen[k] == 0), this test would stay green. Ship's 'every step exactly once' subtest still catches it with mock-only and partial fixtures, but the liverecord test alone does not.

'api_base on 127.0.0.1' and 'api_base on localhost' are also rejected because the create step's https://dev.azure.com evidence is not on the loopback host. So deleting Validate's opening api_base loopback screen leaves TestValidatePostures green. A mock-only fixture with a loopback api_base would pin it. liveStep.texts() already includes Evidence, and Validate also screens Evidence, so ship evidence goes through the loopback screen twice. Harmless.

Several TestValidatePostures cases are rejected by more than one rule, so they don't pin the rule they're named for. 'api_base on 127.0.0.1' and 'api_base on localhost' move api_base off step 0's evidence host, so the evidence rule rejects them too: removing the api_base loopback screen leaves TestValidatePostures green. The shared adoID regex adds 'work item N', so the ship record now accepts evidence like 'work item 41' as naming ADO when it didn't before. That is a small widening of the ship verdict, and no ship test covers it either way.

ship's generic() passes s.texts(), which already includes Evidence, so Validate screens Evidence for loopback twice. It's harmless, but it doesn't match the Step.Texts doc comment ('every other free-text field').

Truncation is detected only by len(value) >= $top (1000). Azure DevOps signals a further page with the x-ms-continuationtoken response header, and adoRequest throws headers away. If the server caps the page below 1000, or pages on its own, a truncated list reads as complete and a protected branch can read as known-unprotected. The worst case is a direct push that gets rejected (TF402455), not a policy bypass.

allowsMergeCommit only falls back to the legacy useSquashMerge field when allowNoFastForward is missing. A modern-form merge-strategy setting that lists only the allowed strategies, e.g. {"allowSquash": true} with no allowNoFastForward key, forbids merge commits in Azure DevOps, but here it reads as allowed=true. If any of allowSquash, allowRebase or allowRebaseMerge is present, a missing allowNoFastForward should mean false. This matters for t-9's auto-complete choice.

TestADOBranchProtectionRefusesHostBeforeRead says Err is the policy refusal but only checks Err != nil, not errors.Is(got.Err, hostallow.ErrRefused). The new hostguard row does assert the refusal, so the gap is covered.

isMergeStrategy also matches the type's displayName 'Require a merge strategy', but azuredevops_ci.go matches policy types by id only. The id match is what counts; the name fallback is harmless but inconsistent.
In TestHermeticBranchProtection_NeverDials, the 'still its gh implementation' message now also covers ADOBranchProtectionFunc, whose real implementation is REST, not gh. Wording only.

The only truncation check in adoBranchPolicies is len(value) >= $top. adoRequest throws away the response headers, so the x-ms-continuationtoken header that Azure DevOps' policy-configurations list uses for paging is never read. If the server returns a smaller page than $top while more entries remain, the list reads as complete and a branch whose policy is cut off reads as Known=true, unprotected. Filtering on the git-scoped endpoint by repositoryId/refName, or checking the continuation header, would close this.

TestADOBranchProtectionReadOnly calls the scope, failure and merge-strategy tests again so its GET-only claim holds whatever -run selects. A full run therefore executes them twice, and adoPolicyMethods is a package-global that keeps growing across tests.

The hostguard branch-policy row checks r.Err rather than r.Reason. The two are the same here because unknown() sets Reason to Err.Error(), so the 'reason without the host refusal' clause is covered by construction.
adoMergeCommitAllowed has no production caller yet; per the record it is groundwork for t-9.

internal/forge/azureboards.go is modified (adoStatusError, the meta cache field, and a second decode-only scrub in doRaw that changes the marker in every decoded 200 body to the bare [redacted]) but is not in the task's declared files list

PathExists passes '.' and '..' segments through url.PathEscape unchanged (e.g. area_path `Web\..` becomes .../Areas/Web/..); a server that normalizes dot segments answers for the parent node, so an invalid configured path reads as present. CheckADOBaseURL already refuses dot segments, so this is a gap compared with that
the meta cache has no lock, so concurrent use of one AzureBoardsClient races on the states map; this is fine while sync is sequential and matches the other clients, none of which use a mutex

full[len(c.project):] in PathExists assumes normalizeADOPath's EqualFold-matched prefix has the same byte length as c.project; a Unicode fold across byte widths (e.g. Kelvin sign vs 'k') could mis-slice or panic. Very unlikely in practice
PathExists reads every 404 as 'missing', including a 404 caused by a wrong [board].project, so doctor would blame the path rather than the project; this matches the test_contract

The mock cleanup checks bypassPolicy only under completionOptions; bypassReason is checked at any depth via findKey. This is enough for the only body the code sends.
